title: Gluing the étale models of a torsor
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme, $G_0$ a sheaf of groups on $X_{\Et}$ and $T$ a
$\nu_X^*G_0$-torsor on $X_{\Proet}$. Then there is a $G_0$-torsor $T_0$ on $X_{\Et}$
and an isomorphism of torsors $\nu_X^*T_0\cong T$, unique up to unique
isomorphism. In particular $T$ is classical and has a trivializing étale
covering.

proof.text: The family of all pro-etale objects equipped with a section of T covers every object, by the local nonemptiness axiom of a comparison torsor. On each member the map g to g times the restricted section is a natural isomorphism from the restricted comparison group sheaf to the restricted T: every component is bijective by simple transitivity.

For a weakly etale site object U, structure-map composition is left adjoint to base change on sites. The induced adjunction on restriction functors identifies pro-etale inverse image along U with sectionwise restriction, by uniqueness of left adjoints. Compose this isomorphism with the canonical etale/pro-etale inverse-image comparison. Therefore restriction of the comparison group sheaf is the comparison inverse image of the etale pullback of its underlying group sheaf.

Thus T is locally classical on the covering from step 1. Apply the general locally-classical descent theorem to obtain an etale set-sheaf model. The essential-image characterization makes T classical and makes its comparison counit invertible. This uses a general sheaf-gluing tool inside the gluing node; it does not change the torsor unit statement or its other proof nodes.

Take S to be the comparison direct image of T. Define the action on S sectionwise using the comparison unit for the group and the original action. Naturality of the unit and its product comparison give the unit, multiplication and restriction laws; its invertibility and simple transitivity give bijectivity. The map from T to the terminal sheaf is epic by local nonemptiness. The invertible counit and terminal comparison identify it with the comparison pullback of the analogous map for S. Faithfulness reflects this epimorphism, and local surjectivity of epimorphisms of set sheaves gives local nonemptiness of S. Naturality and the adjunction triangle show that the counit is equivariant, yielding the constructed etale torsor and ModelIso.

Full faithfulness lifts the quotient of two model isomorphisms uniquely to an etale sheaf isomorphism. Naturality of the product comparison reflects its equivariance, and faithfulness proves uniqueness with the specified model maps. Finally the family of all etale objects with a section of the constructed torsor is jointly surjective, as the nonempty sieve covers the identity etale object. Transport each section by the unit and model isomorphism; simple transitivity gives its natural equivariant trivialization on the whole slice.

proof_origin.place: Gluing and uniqueness, using the generic locally-classical descent tool (Bhatt--Scholze Lemma 5.1.4) in place of repeating its sheaf gluing; explicit action descent by the comparison adjunction.

lean.statement: theorem torsorComparisonGlue (X : Scheme.{u}) (G₀ : Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology GrpCat.{u + 1}) (T : ComparisonTorsor G₀) : (∃ (T₀ : CategoryTheory.Sheaf.NonabelianTorsor.{u, u + 1, u + 1} X G₀) (α : ComparisonTorsor.ModelIso T₀ T), ∀ (T₀' : CategoryTheory.Sheaf.NonabelianTorsor.{u, u + 1, u + 1} X G₀) (α' : ComparisonTorsor.ModelIso T₀' T), ∃! e : T₀.sheaf ≅ T₀'.sheaf, etaleTorsorAction T₀ ≫ e.hom = (𝟙 (groupSets G₀) ⊗ₘ e.hom) ≫ etaleTorsorAction T₀' ∧ (comparisonSets X).map e.hom ≫ α'.iso.hom = α.iso.hom) ∧ IsClassical T.sheaf ∧ ∃ (I : Type (u + 1)) (U : I → X.Etale), (∀ x : X, ∃ (i : I) (y : (U i).left), (U i).hom y = x) ∧ ∀ i : I, Nonempty (ComparisonTorsor.Trivialization T ((Scheme.toProEt X).obj (U i)))
